title: High-Difficulty DI — Multi-Step Computation
tagline: Year 3 — Chains of percentages of percentages: gross profit, operating profit, tax and net profit across companies

introduction.overview: High-difficulty DI sets give data in stages: sales, then costs as a percentage of sales, then expenses as a percentage of sales, then tax as a percentage of profit. A question may need four or five steps in the right order, and each percentage has its own base. The skill is to set up a calculation pipeline once for each row and then reuse it, and to avoid the classic errors of adding percentages with different bases.
introduction.placementRelevance: These multi-step sets are the "hard" end of the DI section in company and management tests.
introduction.realWorldContext: Income statements run exactly this way: revenue, cost of goods, operating costs, tax and net profit.

learningObjectives: Convert each stage to a value before combining
Track the base of every percentage
Compute gross, operating and net profit for each row

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Value = percentage × base ÷ 100. A percentage of a percentage multiplies the fractions.

coreDefinitions: Profit before tax (PBT): gross profit minus operating expenses.
Margin: a profit as a percentage of sales.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Treat each row as a pipeline. Sales flow in, each stage removes a slice, and what remains after the last stage is net profit.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: For each company compute PBT = sales × (100 − COGS% − OPEX%) ÷ 100, then net = PBT × (100 − tax%) ÷ 100. Build a table of these results and answer from it.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Combined
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Sum of nets ÷ sum of sales

mainNarrative: Alfa: sales 800; COGS 50% leaves gross profit 400; operating expenses 10% of sales (80) leave PBT 320; tax 30% of 320 is 96, leaving net profit 224. Net margin = 224 ÷ 800 = 28%.

Beta: sales 600; COGS 60% leaves 240; opex 5% of 600 is 30, so PBT is 210; tax 25% gives net 157.5. Gamma: sales 1,000; COGS 40% leaves 600; opex 150; PBT 450; tax 20% gives net 360. Delta: sales 500; COGS 70% leaves 150; opex 50; PBT 100; tax 30% gives net 70.
Note that COGS and opex are both percentages of sales, but tax is a percentage of PBT. Adding 50% + 10% + 30% is wrong.
Gamma has both the highest net profit (360) and the highest net margin (36%). The margins are Alfa 28%, Beta 26.25%, Gamma 36% and Delta 14%.
For the group, add nets (224 + 157.5 + 360 + 70 = 811.5) and sales (2,900) and divide: 28.0%.

deepDiveAspects.title: Different bases
deepDiveAspects.content: Never add percentages that refer to different bases; convert each to a value first.

deepDiveAspects.title: Sanity check
deepDiveAspects.content: Net profit must be less than PBT, which must be less than gross profit, which must be less than sales.

solvedExamples.title: Pipeline
solvedExamples.question: Alfa has sales ₹800 lakh, COGS 50% and operating expenses 10% of sales, tax 30% of PBT. What is its net profit?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Tax is on PBT, not on sales.

solvedExamples.title: Net margin
solvedExamples.question: Alfa earns net profit ₹224 lakh on sales ₹800 lakh. What is its net margin?

solvedExamples.title: Group margin
solvedExamples.question: The four companies have total net profit ₹811.5 lakh and total sales ₹2,900 lakh. What is the group net margin?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: It is not the average of four margins.

shortcutMethods.title: Row pipeline

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Build gross, PBT and net columns for every row once, then answer by reading or by simple ratios.

rulesForApplication: COGS and opex are on sales.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Net profit must be below PBT.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Compute the three derived columns for all rows first.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Estimate with round numbers to catch slips.

easy.question:
Financial data of four companies (sales in ₹ lakh)

Company | Sales | COGS (% of sales) | Operating expenses (% of sales) | Tax (% of profit before tax)
Alfa | 800 | 50% | 10% | 30%
Beta | 600 | 60% | 5% | 25%
Gamma | 1000 | 40% | 15% | 20%
Delta | 500 | 70% | 10% | 30%

What is the gross profit of Alfa (₹ lakh)?
easy.explanation: Alfa's COGS is 50% of 800, so gross profit = 800 − 400 = 400. The answer is 400.
